first.rationale: Current conditions show activation and onboarding completion both declining QoQ, directly matching the problems that memory_31 and memory_86 addressed successfully. Simplifying onboarding targets the root cause of both metrics. Memory_31 demonstrated durable signup-field reduction for SMB activation; memory_86 showed shortening onboarding lifts adoption. Together these suggest a compound effect. This avoids the retention risk flagged in memory_73 (promotional pricing) while directly addressing measurable degradation. Referral incentives (memory_57) require healthy baseline engagement first. Activation messaging (memory_91) is complementary but secondary to removing friction. Enterprise sales assist (memory_44) doesn't address the SMB volume problem or the QoQ decline. Verification of memory_31 and memory_86 will confirm the magnitude of prior lift and any boundary conditions. Standard experiment scale allows rapid iteration if needed and preserves capacity for follow-up if this shows promise.

final.rationale: Archive confirms simplify_onboarding is the highest-confidence move. Memory_86 showed +13% completion lift with +3% retention gain—directly counters the 4% onboarding completion decline. Memory_31 showed +9% activation with modest -1% retention risk, but only on SMB. Combined, these experiments demonstrate that reducing friction in onboarding and signup drives both activation and completion without retention harm at scale. Current situation shows QoQ declines in both metrics, suggesting friction increase or engagement erosion. Simplifying onboarding addresses root cause rather than masking symptoms. Promotional pricing risks further retention loss per memory_73. Activation messaging alone won't solve the 4% completion decline. This preserves long-term qualified revenue by improving product-market fit signals (time-to-value, completion) rather than artificially stimulating demand. Standard experiment scale allows measurement of SMB-specific effects and comparison to baseline before broader rollout.
